title: Filtered colimits on a Noetherian Zariski site
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian
scheme and $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ a filtered (that is, directed: $I$ is a nonempty directed set, any two elements having a common upper bound) system of abelian sheaves on
[def-sc-zariski-site]. Then

$$
\varinjlim_i H^q(X_{\rm Zar},F_i)
\simeq H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\varinjlim_i F_i)
\quad(q\geq0),
$$

with cohomology as in [def-sc-zariski-cohomology].

proof.text: The underlying topological space of a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. In a Noetherian topological space every open subset is quasi-compact; consequently the quasi-compact opens form a basis (every open is itself quasi-compact) and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact (it is an open subset of a Noetherian space). These are exactly the topological hypotheses required by [lem-sc-topological-filtered-cohomology].

source.place: Lemma 01FF hypotheses, together with Properties Lemma 01OZ and Topology Definition 0051

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-topological-filtered-cohomology] to the underlying topological space of $X$, the system $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ over the directed set $I$ (exactly the index hypothesis of that theorem), and the quasi-compact open $U=X$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_i H^q(X,F_i)\simeq H^q(X,\varinjlim_iF_i)$ for every $q\geq0$. By [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology], cohomology on the open site of the underlying space of a scheme is precisely the cohomology $H^q(X_{\rm Zar},-)$ defined in [def-sc-zariski-cohomology], and the canonical map is the same map induced by the colimit coprojections. This is the asserted isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 01FF conclusion, specialized to the open site of a Noetherian scheme

proof_origin.place: Lemma 01FF (cohomology-lemma-colimit), specialized to the underlying Noetherian topological space of a scheme
